Mike (support): Hey team — Acme is reporting a spike of 503/504s and streaming timeouts from hosted inference since ~09:10 UTC. They see client SDK retry loops and a backlog of half-open streams. Customer says it started after a traffic ramp. Details attached below.

Anika (SRE): Can you paste a sample request/responses and the SDK version? Also region and model they hit.

Mike (support): SDK v1.3.0, region: us-west-2, model: rw-4-large. Customer logs show lots of `upstream 502/504` and `gateway timeout` entries from the edge pods. Example curl they used:```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -d '{"model":"rw-4-large","input":"<prompt>","stream":true}'```

Eli (runtime): Noted. v1.3.0 had an aggressive retry/backoff behavior for streaming that can create connection storms if many clients retry early. Could be hitting connection queue limits on the gateway. Any per-tenant rate spike numbers?

Mike (support): Tess, can you share Acme's recent traffic spike numbers? They reported a 6x increase between 09:05-09:12 UTC.

Tess (account): Confirmed. Traffic auto-scaled on their side; peak concurrent streams ~1.8k for that window. They were previously at ~300. They say retries began when first ~1000 streams opened.

Anika (SRE): Hypothesis: gateway connection queue exhausted -> backend starts returning 502/504 -> SDK clients immediately retry -> thundering herd. Also streaming sockets held open longer when KV cache miss + long generations. Two quick probes we should run: 1) Check gateway queue metrics (conn queue length, accept drops) 2) Inspect edge pod logs for `accept rate exceeded` or `keepalive timeout`. I can pull metrics now.

sre-bot: alert: EDGE_CONN_QUEUE_HIGH for tenant acme-corp at 2023-09-14T09:11:34Z (p95 queue length 2200)

Anika (SRE): Pulled traces — we saw many connections getting into a timed-wait state and large Q length. Backend nodes accept latency jumped at same time. Also found a small percentage of responses with `504 upstream read timeout` from the reverse proxy.

Eli (runtime): On runtime side there are two likely contributory factors: 1) Continuous batching + long-tokens meant peers held GPU workers longer, reducing throughput per worker. 2) SDK retry jitter settings in v1.3.0 can retry on chunked timeouts rather than full-request failures. We should recommend customers upgrade to SDK v1.4.2 which has streaming retry smoothing.

Mike (support): Customer asked for immediate mitigation — what can we do now operationally to reduce impact while we fix root cause?

Anika (SRE): Mitigations we can apply quickly: - Enable tenant soft-throttle on ingress to smooth new connection acceptance (rate limit new connections per second) - Route excess traffic to fallback model (rw-4-medium) for best-effort continuity - Increase proxy keepalive and reduce connection timeout to free stale sockets faster - Temporarily bump edge pool capacity (scale-out) if GPUs available

Eli (runtime): I can push a short-lived config to reduce max continuous batch window from 1.2s to 0.6s for this tenant to free workers faster. Also can change our KV cache eviction policy to reduce holding long-running workers for cache-miss tails.

Tess (account): I'll request customer to enable client-side exponential backoff and upgrade to SDK v1.4.2. Offering them temporary free burst capacity and notify them of a recommended concurrency cap of 800 concurrent streams until we stabilize.

Mike (support): Sent Acme an update: "We're applying ingress smoothing, routing excess to rw-4-medium, and pushing runtime config changes. Please upgrade SDK to v1.4.2 and cap concurrent streams to 800 for the next 2 hours. We'll follow up once metrics look healthy." :thumbsup:

Anika (SRE): Actions I've taken: applied tenant soft-throttle (new conn rps -> 350, smoothing window 60s) and scaled edge ASG +2 instances. Observed queue length dropping from 2200 -> 520 in 6 minutes.

Eli (runtime): Pushed runtime change: continuous batch window 0.6s for tenant acme-corp and enabled shorter batch timeouts. Backend worker utilization returned to normal and tail latencies reduced. No rollbacks.

sre-bot: incident note created: INCIDENT-2023-09-14-ACME-SPIKE. Postmortem assigned to Anika + Eli.

Mike (support): Customer reply: "Thanks — latency and errors dropping. We'll roll SDK update now and keep traffic capped." They attached a short client log showing fewer 5xxs.

Tess (account): Customer accepted the temporary credits. Scheduling follow-up call for 16:00 UTC to discuss long-term options: Dedicated capacity or rate-aware routing.

Anika (SRE): Next steps (action list): - Full postmortem (Anika/Eli) - Add recommended SDK backoff defaults to support KB and SDK release notes (Eli) - Consider automatic tenant-level soft-throttle when queue > threshold (Anika) - Explore proactive routing to cheaper fallback models on surge (product discussion)

Mike (support): Closing note: Please add any additional observations. I will keep thread open until postmortem is published. Thanks all for quick triage. :party-parrot:
